To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spatio-temporal characteristics of remote sensing products are important to FEWS NET decision makers and that rainfall and vegetative data products are valued as FEWS NET inputs.

(i) FEWS NET end-users have a wide range of requirements for biophysical data, (ii) these requirements vary by location, time of year, and type of hazard, (iii) the most important requirements are for high spatial resolution data and for data that can provide actionable food security and humanitarian information, (iv) rainfall products and vegetation products are most highly valued, (v) the most important temporal resolution is daily, and (vi) the most important spatial resolution is sub-k

FEWS NET end users have a strong preference for high resolution remote sensing data, and that the spatio-temporal resolutions of rainfall and vegetation products must be flexible to meet the needs of the FEWS NET end-users.
